analysis.title: Americas Asset Managers: 3Q26 EPS Wrap-up: KKR and AMG
key_insights: GS raises its 2026 ANI per share estimate for KKR to $8.40 from $8.02, mostly on a strong 3Q. It lowers 2027/28 to $7.29/$8.74 from $7.53/$8.90.

The KKR 2027/28 cuts come from about $140mn a year of lost Strategic Holdings dividends after recent sales (KKR expects to recover about 50% by 2028) and from lower PRE after a softer 4Q update and lower NAC balances.

GS FRE estimates for KKR are largely unchanged. Drivers are Global Infra, Asia Infra and Helix in Real Assets, Asia V and Arctos/KKR Solutions in PE, private IG/ABF and third-party credit (KKR expects a record year), and K-Series growth in wealth.
GS sees 2027E organic, ex-catch-up management fee growth of about 15% at KKR, versus about 20% currently running on a trailing basis as of 3Q26.
KKR trades at 14X 2027 P/E (net of SBC), which GS calls attractive. The balance-sheet-heavy model remains the investor concern and an overhang on valuation.

KKR 3Q26 firmwide management fees were $1.20bn, in line with GSe and slightly below the Street. Excluding catch-up fees and pro forma for Arctos, they grew about 1-2% sequentially. GS models $1.24bn for 4Q26E.

KKR Private Equity: Arctos integration is ahead of plan. Keystone closed at about $6bn, the largest first-time GP solutions fund. A GP-led secondaries strategy follows in 2027, and management sees KKR Solutions reaching $100bn+ of AUM over time.

KKR Real Assets: Global Infra final close was $19.2bn versus about $17bn for its predecessor. Helix commitments exceed $11bn. APAC Infra III is still raising, and GS models about $9bn versus $6.4bn for the prior fund, which should add catch-up fees into year-end.

KKR AI exposure: about $45bn of digital infra equity and about $40bn of power equity deployed. The seven data center platforms are about 6% of infra AUM, or 1-2% of firm AUM including Global Atlantic. About 90% of leases are to governments or investment-grade hyperscalers and about 3% to neoclouds.
KKR transaction and monitoring fees and FRPR both beat GSe, helped by a pickup in capital markets activity and growing perpetual K-Series and infrastructure contributions.
KKR Strategic Holdings contributed $192mn in 3Q versus GSe $115mn. GS cuts 4Q26E to $85mn from $150mn and 2027E to $320mn from $480mn. Management still points to about $350mn for full-year 2026.
GS stays Buy on KKR and raises its 12-month target to $131 from $125 on a SOTP framework, rolling one quarter forward. Downside risks are lower investment marks and slower exits.

AMG: GS raises 2026/27/28 EPS to $39.11/$47.20/$56.31 from $37.52/$45.18/$53.81, on stronger 3Q core EBITDA, a higher recurring FRE run-rate into 4Q, a larger 2026 buyback and higher 4Q performance fees, partly offset by 4Q mark-to-market headwinds (blended down 2% through Nov 6).
Management now expects 2026 economics EPS growth of about 50%, up from about 40% in 2Q, with alternatives contributing about 70%.

AMG's tax-aware long/short strategies kept growing despite SCHW capping new accounts and IRS/Treasury questions about parts of the ecosystem. Management saw no evidence of flows pulled forward into 3Q and expects low turnover from existing clients.

AMG flows are broad. Private markets show about 20% LTM organic growth, liquid alternatives nearly 40%, and the non-tax-aware part of the business 14%. EBITDA contribution from flows runs about 2x the asset-based organic growth rate, with operating leverage beyond AQR at Pantheon and other affiliates.
AMG 3Q net inflows were $20.7bn (about 9% annualized organic growth), with alternative affiliates at $31.5bn. Liquid alternatives added $21.9bn and private markets $9.6bn.

AMG 3Q adjusted EBITDA was $354mn (+41% y/y), well ahead of the $315mn-$325mn guide. 4Q guide is $405mn-$475mn of adjusted EBITDA, built from recurring FRE of $335mn-$345mn and $70mn-$130mn of net performance fees. GS models 4Q adjusted EBITDA of $465mn.

AMG capital return: $400mn repurchased in 3Q, $775mn YTD (about 9% of shares outstanding). The 2026 buyback guide rises to >$900mn, and GS models about $975mn. Shares outstanding are down about 30% since the start of 2024.

Management expects cumulative free cash flow over the next 5-7 years to approximate today's market cap, which GS says the stock's valuation does not capture. GS sees about 10% upside to Visible Alpha consensus EPS in 2027 and 2028 and, at about 8.2X 2027 P/E, more than 30% upside to its target.

GS stays Buy on AMG and raises its 12-month target to $451 from $426 on about 8X Q5-Q8 P/E (unchanged). Downside risks are deterioration in long-only equity strategies, equity market declines and M&A execution.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $131 from $125 on SOTP and a one-quarter roll forward. GS says balance-sheet intensity remains an overhang on valuation.
Target raised to $451 from $426 on about 8X Q5-Q8 P/E. EPS estimates rise on stronger EBITDA, a larger buyback and higher performance fees.

sector_views.rationale: Both names are Buy rated. Fee growth in infrastructure, credit, secondaries and wealth vehicles, and strong flows in private markets and liquid alternatives, support earnings.

earnings_insights: KKR 3Q26 firmwide management fees $1.20bn reported, vs GSe $1.21bn and Visible Alpha Street consensus $1.22bn.
KKR 3Q26 PE management fees $466mn reported (+18% Y/Y). Real Assets management fees $395mn reported (+13% Y/Y).
KKR 3Q26 net transaction and monitoring fees $328mn reported vs GSe $288mn (+48% Q/Q, flat Y/Y). FRPR $326mn reported vs GSe $280mn and $73mn in 3Q25.
KKR 3Q26 Strategic Holdings contribution $192mn reported vs GSe $115mn. GS estimate for 4Q26E cut to $85mn from $150mn and 2027E to $320mn from $480mn.

GS ANI per share estimates for KKR (estimates, not reported): 2026 $8.40 (from $8.02), 2027 $7.29 (from $7.53), 2028 $8.74 (from $8.90). GS models 4Q26E management fees of $1.24bn (+3% Q/Q), 2026/27E transaction fees of $1.14bn/$1.43bn and FRPR of $638mn/$684mn.

AMG 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA $354mn reported (+41% y/y) vs company guide of $315mn-$325mn. Recurring FRE $325mn reported vs $315mn guided, net performance fees $14mn reported vs up to $10mn guided, catch-up fees $15mn reported.

AMG 4Q26 company guidance (not yet reported): adjusted EBITDA $405mn-$475mn (midpoint $440mn), recurring FRE $335mn-$345mn, net performance fees $70mn-$130mn, Economic EPS $11.37-$13.43 on 25.1mn shares. GS models 4Q adjusted EBITDA $465mn and Economic EPS $13.09.

AMG 2026 Economic EPS implied by guidance midpoint is about $38.25, about 50% y/y growth. GS 2026/27/28 EPS estimates are $39.11/$47.20/$56.31, and GS sees about 10% upside to Visible Alpha consensus in 2027 and 2028.
AMG repurchased $400mn of stock in 3Q26 (reported) vs $189mn in 2Q. YTD buybacks $775mn. 2026 guide raised to >$900mn from about $600mn, and GS models about $975mn.

tension_points.bull_case: Diversified model drives healthy FRE and PRE growth despite macro challenges, the balance sheet has produced recent gains, and the stock trades at 14X 2027 P/E (net of SBC).
tension_points.bear_case: The balance-sheet-heavy model remains an investor concern and an overhang on valuation, and lost Strategic Holdings dividends of about $140mn a year cut 2027/28 ANI per share.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lower marks on the investment portfolio or slower exits, the downside risks GS names.

tension_points.bull_case: L/S tax-aware strategies kept growing, with no sign of flows pulled forward into 3Q, low expected turnover and expanding custodian offerings.
tension_points.bear_case: SCHW is capping new accounts and IRS/Treasury are questioning parts of the ecosystem, so the tax-aware debate intensified this quarter.
